title: Adaptive stub-backend and latency-governor playbook for downstream failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe tail latency and availability regressions when Redis or Kafka in a region experiences saturation or transient errors. Existing strategies (hedging, connection trimming) are effective but require manual tuning per-service and do not cover mixed-criticality responses. Goal: Implement an operational playbook and implementation of two complementary controls: (1) an adaptive stub-backend layer that can return lightweight, deterministic degraded responses for non-critical request paths (embeddings cache misses, non-blocking logs, downstream analytic writes), and (2) a latency-governor that uses continuous P50/P95/P99 deltas to auto-adjust connection-slim settings, admission controls, and shedding thresholds per-tenant and per-route. Deliverables: design doc, runtime change, a small proxy/stub service, CI tests, and a runbook with dashboards and escalation steps.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook documented with clear decision tree: when to route to stub-backend vs retry vs fail-fast
Latency-governor implemented and enabled behind feature flag; can be toggled per-region and per-environment
Automated experiments (dark traffic) show governor reduces P99 by >20% during injected downstream saturation without increasing global error rate >0.05%
Stub-backend returns semantically correct degraded payloads for 95% of non-critical paths and logs sampled payloads for audit
End-to-end e2e tests and chaos test scenarios (redis-kill, kafka-latency-inject) added to CI that validate graceful degradation behavior
Runbook and alerting integrated into Console: recommended dashboards, SLO play thresholds, and post-incident checklist
notes: Design trade-off: full response synthesis (models) vs fast deterministic stubs. We choose deterministic stubs for predictability and cost reasons; model-based fallbacks can be considered as a follow-up for higher fidelity degradations.
We will prioritize non-blocking writes and read-only flows for stubbing. Critical auth and billing paths must never be stubbed and are subject to stricter admission rules.
Governor parameters (token-bucket sizes, connection-slim target, admission window) will be seeded from historical telemetry and auto-tuned during shadow runs before enabling wide rollout.
Coordination: requires changes in runtime (connection admission), proxy layer (routing to stub), and Console (toggles and dashboards).
steps: 1) Draft playbook and detailed decision tree (done)
2) Implement stub-backend prototype and integrate with proxy routing (PR 8421)
3) Add latency-governor control loop to runtime with feature flag + metrics export
4) Run dark-traffic experiments for 2 weeks, collect telemetry for auto-tuning
5) Add CI chaos tests and e2e tests validating response semantics
6) Gradual rollout: staging -> canary (5% traffic) -> regional 50% -> global; monitor SLOs and abort criteria
7) Publish runbook and schedule on-call training session
